jobs.title: Head of Operations @ Koast.ai
jobs.description:
Headquarters: Tampa, Florida
    
URL: https://koast.ai


Head of Operations | Full-time | Remote (US hours) | Reports to the CEO | Growth path to VP of Operations / COO
Koast is the AI operating layer for teams that run Meta ads at volume. Agencies, in-house media buying teams, and enterprise buyers managing 10+ ad accounts and launching 50+ ads a week use Koast to launch faster, automate optimizations off real attribution data, and see every account from one Command Center. The Koast Agent is the next layer: an AI that reads the account, spots what matters, and acts inside guardrails.
We are bootstrapped, profitable, and growing faster than our processes. Customers are onboarding weekly through direct sales and partnerships, contractors span three time zones, and the CEO is still the person who notices when an invoice did not go out or a new customer never got their onboarding call. That stops with this hire.
You will be one of the first ten full-time employees at Koast. You will own how the company runs so the CEO can own where it goes. You are the anchor between engineering, support, customer success, and sales: the person who makes sure the vision the CEO sets actually gets executed, at a high standard, across every function.
This is not a back-office seat. You will live inside the product. You will know the launch flow, the Command Center, and the Agent well enough to run a customer onboarding yourself, reproduce a bug before you file it, and tell engineering which support ticket is a one-off and which one is a pattern.
What you will own
The anchor between functions. Sales promises something, engineering ships something, support hears about the gap. You sit in the middle of all four and close it. You will own the handoffs (sales to onboarding, support to engineering, engineering to customer success), make sure each team knows what the others are doing, and turn the CEO's priorities into a plan each function can execute this week.
The operating cadence. Weekly priorities, the metrics review, the state-of-the-union thread, the quarterly plan. You will build the rhythm the company runs on and make sure every function knows what it owes and when.
Revenue operations. The pipeline from lead to paid to renewed. GoHighLevel, Stripe, Granola, and the automations that tie them together. Clean data, accurate MRR and churn, a sales rep who never has to ask "where does this deal go."
Customer operations. Onboarding, support triage in Intercom, escalations, renewals, and the handoff from sales to success. Every enterprise account gets a named owner, a kickoff, and a 30-day check-in, and you will know which ones are at risk before they tell us.
People and contractors. Hiring pipelines, contractor agreements, onboarding docs, payroll and payouts, performance check-ins. As we go from a handful of contractors to a real team, you will build the system that makes each new person productive in their first week.
Finance operations. Bookkeeping hygiene, monthly close with our accountant, cash forecasting, vendor and tool spend, partner payouts (Whop, affiliates, referral partners). Not the CFO seat. The person who makes sure the numbers are right and the CEO sees them on the first of the month.
Partnerships and vendors. Contracts, renewals, compliance items (Meta platform terms, data policies), and the operational side of partnerships like Whop and Flex: who owes what, by when, and whether it happened.
Systems and automation. You will look at every recurring manual task and ask whether Zapier, an internal tool, or an AI agent should be doing it instead. Then you will build it or spec it for someone who can.
What you will do week to week
Run the weekly ops review: pipeline, churn, cash, hiring, blockers. One page, numbers first.
Use Koast every day. Run onboardings in it, triage support tickets against it, and bring engineering the patterns, not the anecdotes.
Translate the CEO's quarterly priorities into a plan with owners and dates across sales, support, success, and engineering, then hold each function to it.
Own the onboarding calendar for new customers and new hires so nothing waits on the CEO.
Keep the sales pipeline, CRM, and billing in sync and catch the exceptions before they become refund requests.
Draft and manage contractor agreements, vendor contracts, and partner order forms.
Close the books monthly with our bookkeeper and flag anything that looks wrong.
Build the automation or the SOP for any task you have done more than twice.
Write the updates: one for the CEO, one for the team, one for the partner. Each one short.
Say "we do not need this tool" and cancel it.
What sets you apart
You have been the operator behind a founder at a company that went from 5 to 50 people, or from $1M to $10M, and you built the systems that made that possible.
You know performance marketing or agency operations from the inside. You understand why a media buyer cares about a delayed ad account approval and what it costs when onboarding slips a week.
You are fluent in the modern ops stack (CRM, billing, bookkeeping, contracts, automation) and you configure it yourself rather than waiting on a consultant.
You are hands-on with software. You learn a product deeply, you can read a Shortcut ticket and a PostHog funnel, and engineers trust you to bring them a real problem instead of a forwarded complaint.
You have sat between sales, support, and engineering before and kept all three moving in the same direction without being the boss of any of them.
You bring numbers to every conversation and you are comfortable telling the CEO the number he does not want to hear.
You write tightly. Your SOPs are shorter than everyone else's and people actually follow them.
You are comfortable owning things nobody assigned you, and comfortable letting go of them when it is time to hire someone better.
Requirements
5+ years in operations, revenue operations, or chief-of-staff roles at a B2B SaaS or agency, including at least one early-stage or high-growth environment.
Hands-on experience with a CRM (GoHighLevel, HubSpot, or similar), Stripe or comparable billing, and QuickBooks or comparable bookkeeping.
Experience managing contractors and vendors, including drafting and negotiating agreements.
Familiarity with Meta ads, agency workflows, or ad-tech is strongly preferred.
Demonstrated experience working directly with a software product and an engineering team: filing and prioritizing tickets, running QA or UAT, and using product analytics to make decisions.
Comfortable with Zapier, Make, or scripting light automations. Experience directing AI tools or agents to do operational work is a plus.
Available full-time during US business hours.
How You Work
Small team, high trust, no theater. Decisions are made with numbers, written down, and revisited when the numbers change. These are the values we run on. If they sound like you, you will fit right in.
Mastery. "Good enough" is where you start, not where you stop. You keep sharpening the craft: tighter systems, cleaner numbers, fewer surprises.
Push the Boundaries. You take on the ambitious version of the problem. Most ops teams manage the chaos. You want to build the company that does not have it.
Embrace the Challenge. When a customer's onboarding breaks at 9pm, you are in the thread, not waiting for the morning standup.
Responsibility. You own your commitments. If a date slips, everyone hears it from you first, with a new date attached.
Dedication. You dive into the hard, unglamorous problems (messy books, a broken handoff, a contract nobody read) and iterate until they are solved.
Collaboration. You write clearly, share what you learn, and make sales, engineering, and customers faster for having worked with you.
Why Koast
Early-stage impact. You will be one of the first ten full-time employees. How this company runs at 50 people will be the system you built at 10.
AI and ads at scale. You will operate at the frontier of AI-driven media buying, alongside some of the highest-volume ad teams on Meta.
Real upside. Bootstrapped and profitable, so the equity means something. Full-time salary, performance bonuses, paid time off, and a vested equity grant that grows with the seat as you move toward VP of Operations or COO.
Remote and flexible. Work from anywhere, on your schedule, during US hours. Just make sure the machine runs.
How to apply
Record a Loom, five minutes or less, covering these five things in order:
Show us a system you built. Screen-share a process, dashboard, or automation you designed that the company still uses. Walk us through why it exists and what it replaced.
One thing you would kill. A process, tool, or meeting you inherited and shut down, and what happened after.
One number. A metric you owned, where it was when you started, where it was when you left, and what you changed.
One handoff you fixed. A time sales, support, and engineering were not aligned, what it was costing, and how you closed the gap.
Where Koast fits. Sixty seconds on what breaks first when a bootstrapped SaaS company doubles headcount, and what you would do in your first 30 days here to prevent it.
Email the Loom link and your LinkedIn or resume to jobs@koast.ai with the subject line "Scaling with Koast".
No cover letters. We watch the Loom first and read the resume second. Applications without the video are not reviewed.
To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/koast-ai-head-of-operations-koast-ai

jobs.title: Billing Systems Architect
jobs.description:
Headquarters: Remote • Anywhere


About Upsun (formerly Platform.sh) 
Upsun is the cloud application platform humans and robots love. It is built for today’s hybrid teams, where AI agents write and test code and humans focus on solving the problems that really matter. Developers, DevOps engineers, and platform teams use Upsun to build, ship, and scale confidently without wrestling with backend infrastructure. We give you your time back. You get:
Predictable performance, even at scale 
Secure, compliant environments by default 
Real-time observability and profiling built in 
Cloning, configuration, and provisioning in seconds 
AI-ready features that plug directly into your stack 
The name says it all. "Up" means uptime, reliability, and acceleration. "Sun" reflects our follow-the-sun-support, a 24x7, globally distributed support team keeping the lights on while you rest. Our core belief is that software should power brighter solutions and greater innovation. 
Upsunners are a remote, global workforce, and we thrive in a multicultural team. We are committed to open source and an open, welcoming environment. Our team spans the globe and the experience spectrum. 
What's our commonality, our cultural fabric? A curious spirit and a thirst for knowledge; an eagerness for innovative ideas and cultures. We believe we can build anything together in an environment that frees you to do your best work. 
Our values: 
 We make a positive impact.
 We aim for the stars.
 We care for each other. 
Impact of a Billing Systems Architect
As an Enterprise Billing Systems Architect at Upsun, you are the technical anchor of our billing infrastructure, playing a vital role in ensuring our revenue operations, pricing structures, and financial integrations run seamlessly as our business scales. Picking up primary ownership from our implementation partner, you serve as the dedicated technical lead bridging Finance, Product, and Engineering.
You’re deeply analytical, systems-minded, and collaborative—someone who thrives on translating complex business, pricing, and accounting rules into reliable system logic. Working downstream from our core engineering and data mediation teams, you ensure the integrity of our Quote-to-Cash (Q2C) platform while continuously optimizing platform performance and automation.
Beyond day-to-day platform administration, you contribute to the long-term evolution of our billing architecture—supporting new pricing model launches, complex usage rating schemes, and financial system integrations. Your attention to detail, technical versatility, and cross-functional mindset ensure our revenue pipeline remains scalable, compliant, and friction-free.
What to expect
Billing Infrastructure & Administration: Serve as the hands-on technical owner of our BillingPlatform environment, configuring catalogs, price cards, usage rating rules, and automated invoice schedules.
System Operations & Maintenance: Own ongoing platform health, including system updates, pricing launches, recurring bill-run troubleshooting, sync exception handling, and root-cause issue resolution.
Data Ingestion & Analysis: Utilize SQL to perform data validation, rating engine auditing, and operational reporting while collaborating with Engineering to receive mediated usage data (e.g., via DigitalRoute or Kafka).
Integrations & API Management: Maintain and optimize clean, API-driven integrations connecting BillingPlatform to upstream CRMs (e.g. Salesforce), downstream ERP/GL tools (e.g., NetSuite), and payment gateways (e.g., Stripe).
Revenue Recognition Alignment: Partner closely with Accounting to ensure system rating rules, revenue schedules, and general ledger mappings satisfy ASC 606 and IFRS 15 compliance standards.
Cross-Functional Collaboration: Gather technical and operational requirements directly from Accounting, Finance, Sales Ops, and Product teams, translating their vision into sustainable platform configuration.
Data Integrity & Migration: Maintain billing data continuity and manage subscription data updates or migrations without disrupting ongoing financial operations or revenue recognition flows.
What you bring
Q2C Platform Experience: Proven hands-on experience configuring and administering enterprise Quote-to-Cash or billing platforms (e.g., Zuora, Salesforce Revenue Cloud/CPQ, NetSuite Billing, Aria Systems, or BillingPlatform).
Data & Technical Skills: Strong proficiency with SQL for querying and auditing billing data, alongside a solid grasp of REST APIs, webhooks, and ETL workflows.
Modern Pricing Expertise: Experience supporting complex SaaS or infrastructure pricing models—such as PLG, hybrid commitment-plus-usage, tiered rates, and consumption-based/metered billing.
Revenue Recognition Knowledge: Practical understanding of rev rec fundamentals (ASC 606 / IFRS 15) and how accounting rules dictate billing engine design.
Cross-Functional Communication: Ability to bridge technical language and financial business logic, effectively collaborating with engineering teams and accounting stakeholders alike.
Problem Solving & Troubleshooting: A methodical approach to diagnosing system sync errors, rating anomalies, and integration edge cases to ensure operational continuity.
 
Bonus points
Experience with DigitalRoute mediation software or Kafka event-stream data intake
Previous exposure to cloud infrastructure, PaaS, or developer-platform usage metrics
Background supporting system migrations from implementation partners into internal teams
Where we hire
At Upsun, remote work isn't just a trend - it's our foundation. The freedom of remote work with the support of a diverse, global team has been our successful model for over a decade. Our culture celebrates flexibility and collaboration, and while we have team members in over 30 countries around the globe, we are currently focused on hiring for this role in Australia, Canada, France, Germany, Spain, the United Kingdom, and the United States. Although we’re unable to provide visa sponsorship at this time, we welcome applications from all qualified candidates who are legally authorized to work in these countries. 
How we hire
We know that a great hire won’t meet every requirement that we’ve outlined. If you can see yourself elevating the team, we want to hear your story. Few of us would be here had we not taken a chance.   
You can expect 5 video interviews on Google Meet to follow the order below. Should you successfully move through the entire process you will have the opportunity to meet with a variety of Upsunners. Our goal is to ensure you can make the most informed decision on whether this role, and our culture aligns with what you’re looking for in your future working environment. 
45 Minutes with Talent Acquisition 
60 Minutes with Hiring Manager (Senior Director, FP&A and IT)
60 Minutes with Team (Engineering team)
60 Minutes with Team (Finance team)

45 Minutes with Executive (CFO)
All roles require background checks.
What we offer
 A product you can believe in - Join us in transforming how businesses build and manage web applications, driven making a positive impact as a proud B Corp.
 An Award-Winning Workplace - We’ve been recognized by Forbes’ Top 30 Companies for Remote Jobs and France’s Best Workplaces for Women.
️ A culture that values your voice - Join a flexible, open, and inclusive work environment where your voice is encouraged, and your ideas shape our growth and evolution.
 A global team - Collaborate with colleagues from diverse backgrounds across the world, embracing different perspectives
 Benefits and perks - Make the most of what matters to you
 Flexible PTO
 Comprehensive healthcare coverage (UK, Canada, France, Spain, USA)
 Company stock options
 Professional development budget
 Office equipment budget
‍️ Wellness budget
 Annual team gatherings
 Internet reimbursement
 Inclusive parental leave
️ Remote work travel program
You belong here
At Upsun, we celebrate diversity in all its forms and are committed to fostering an inclusive, equitable, and supportive workplace where everyone can thrive. We embrace and value different perspectives, backgrounds, and experiences, because they make us stronger as a team. Whoever you are, wherever you're from, and whatever path you've taken, you are welcome here. We encourage you to bring your whole self to work, connect with others, and share your passion. If you need accommodations at any stage of our hiring process, please let us know. We're here to ensure an accessible and comfortable experience for you.

Fastly helps people stay better connected with the things they love. Fastly’s edge cloud platform enables customers to create great digital experiences quickly, securely, and reliably by processing, serving, and securing our customers’ applications as close to their end-users as possible — at the edge of the Internet. The platform is designed to take advantage of the modern internet, to be programmable, and to support agile software development. Fastly’s customers include many of the world’s most prominent companies, including GitHub, Yelp, Paramount, and JetBlue.
We're building a more trustworthy Internet. Come join us.

Senior SRE - Networks
Fastly’s Technical Operations (TechOps) team is responsible for building & operating the infrastructure that powers the Fastly Edge Cloud Platform. We oversee an extensive global network that spans 6 continents with over 100 points of presence and 578 Tbps of connected capacity.  Our platform serves a significant portion of the content delivered to internet consumers across the planet, with customers ranging from online media streaming services to e-commerce, to open source projects, nonprofits and more. We’re looking for an experienced SRE with strong focus on Networks, SRE principals and knowledge of the internet who can bring engineering best practices, operational rigour, and automation skills to help craft the future of Fastly’s network and directly contribute to making the internet better.
What You'll Do:
Build, operate, and maintain the continually growing global network footprint of Fastly’s Edge Cloud Platform.

Experience in Automation and coding using languages like Python, or similar.

Experience working with alerting, monitoring and visibility tools (such as Graphite/Grafana, Prometheus, or Splunk).

Experience in network telemetry including instrumenting infrastructure and collecting, processing, storing and analyzing data

jobs.description:
Headquarters: Remote - Abu Dhabi



Ready to do the most impactful work of your career? At Coinbase, we are uncompromising on our mission to increase economic freedom. The bar is high, the environment is intense, and we like it that way. This isn't a place for complacency, it’s a place to be pushed past your perceived limits. If you're ready to build the future of finance alongside people who refuse to settle for "good enough," you belong here. Coinbase is a remote-first, but not remote-only company. Expect to get together quarterly for intense in-person working sessions called “surges.” learn more about working at Coinbase.

Coinbase Tokenized Equities give eligible non-US users a simple way to buy tokens backed 1:1 by US stocks and ETFs — no brokerage account needed. The tokens are issued out of Abu Dhabi Global Market (ADGM), a regulated financial center overseen by the FSRA, and trade 24/7 onchain. We're hiring an Accounting Manager to be the finance lead for this product. This is a senior individual contributor role for someone who likes to build. You'll own the accounting and reporting model from the ground up — accounting policy, regulatory and legal entity reporting, controls, GL operations, and finance systems — coordinating across Tax, Treasury, FP&A, and controllership, as well as external auditors and regulators. If you like solving hard problems and building from scratch, this role is for you.
What You'll Do
Build the accounting model from the ground up — covering token issuance and redemption, asset tracking, intercompany flows, and the close process
Own regulatory compliance and reporting to the FSRA for this business. This includes liaising with the regulator to ensure a consistent understand of the rules, building a robust, efficient and well controlled reporting process and remaining responsive ad hoc queries
Partner with Product, Engineering, Legal, Tax, Compliance, Treasury, FP&A, and Finance Data so new flows are accurate, controlled, and scalable
Sign off on flow of funds, posting rules, account setup, ledger structure, reconciliations, and reporting before launch
Lead accounting analysis for new structures under US GAAP and IFRS, including dividends, splits, and balance sheet treatment
Build the reporting framework for our issuer entity, including annual audited IFRS financials, local filings, and external audit support
Set up a control environment for a regulated launch — audit trails, books and records, and data integrity across on-chain and off-chain systems
Identify accounting, controls, and reporting risks early and ensure each has a clear owner and plan
Required Skills
A degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field; CPA, CA, or similar strongly preferred
Strong accounting or finance experience in a regulated setting (capital markets, broker-dealer, exchange, custody, clearing, or digital assets)
Experience working directly with a financial regulator — inquiries, exams, or filings
Proven ability to apply accounting rules to new or complex products
Experience building new finance processes for a new product, entity, or regulatory regime
A strong controls mindset and the ability to shape how systems are built before launch
Clear communication skills and comfort in ambiguous, fast-moving environments

jobs.description:

We don't just provide health insurance—we deliver the kind of healthcare that people deserve. The Actuarial team at Clover combines rigorous analytics with innovative technology to solve complex healthcare challenges and improve outcomes for our members. Our actuaries play a critical role in driving financial performance, evaluating business strategies, and helping shape the future of Medicare Advantage.
We're looking for a highly analytical and intellectually curious Actuarial Analyst to join Clover's actuarial rotational program. This role is designed to provide broad exposure to multiple actuarial disciplines while building a strong technical foundation in Medicare Advantage.
As an Actuarial Analyst, you'll work alongside experienced actuaries and business leaders on projects spanning financial forecasting, reserving, medical economics, pricing, value-based care, revenue and risk adjustment analysis, and operational strategy. Through rotational assignments, you'll develop a comprehensive understanding of the Medicare Advantage business while building the analytical, technical, and business skills needed for long-term success.
This role is ideal for candidates who enjoy solving challenging problems, working with large datasets, and using quantitative analysis to influence business decisions.
As an Actuarial Analyst, you will:
Perform quantitative analyses that support key actuarial functions, including financial forecasting, medical cost analysis, revenue optimization, reserving, pricing, risk adjustment, and value-based care initiatives.
Develop and maintain analytical models using actuarial principles, statistical methods, and large healthcare datasets to evaluate financial performance, identify trends, and support strategic decision-making.
Partner with actuaries and cross-functional business leaders to analyze operational and financial performance, investigate emerging trends, and develop data-driven recommendations.
Prepare reports, dashboards, and executive presentations that communicate complex analytical findings and support business planning, forecasting, and performance monitoring.
Support enterprise financial planning by analyzing medical costs, revenue drivers, risk adjustment performance, utilization trends, and other key business metrics across the Medicare Advantage business.
Identify opportunities to improve processes and automate analyses using SQL, Excel, Python, and other AI analytical tools.
Participate in rotational assignments across multiple actuarial disciplines to develop broad business knowledge and technical expertise while contributing to strategic initiatives across the organization.
Support special projects and innovation initiatives that improve healthcare affordability, operational performance, member outcomes, and enterprise financial results.
Success in this role looks like
In your first 90 days, you will: Build relationships across the Actuarial organization and become familiar with Clover's Medicare Advantage business. Learn Clover's analytical tools, financial models, and reporting processes. Contribute to recurring analyses while developing a strong understanding of actuarial methodologies and business operations.
After 6 months, you will: Independently own recurring analyses and deliver accurate, timely insights to support business decision-making. Develop technical expertise in actuarial modeling, healthcare analytics, and financial forecasting. Successfully complete your first rotational assignment while building relationships across multiple actuarial functions.
Future success in this role includes: Becoming a trusted analytical partner to business leaders and cross-functional teams. Developing expertise across multiple actuarial disciplines before transitioning into a specialized role. Continuing progress toward actuarial credentials while building a long-term career at Clover.
You should get in touch if you have:
Experience: 2-4 years of experience in healthcare finance, analytics, actuarial, consulting, strategy, operations, or a related field. Successful completion of one or more Society of Actuaries (SOA) exams is required.
Industry Knowledge: Experience in Medicare Advantage, managed care, or value-based healthcare preferred.
Analytical Skills: Strong quantitative, analytical, and problem-solving skills with the ability to work with large datasets and complex business questions.
Technical Skills: SQL and Excel skills required; experience with Python, R, AI tools, Github, and business intelligence platforms preferred.
Communication: Strong communication and presentation skills with the ability to translate complex analyses into actionable business insights.

Additionally, we embrace a remote-first culture that supports collaboration and flexibility, allowing our team members to thrive from any location.

About Clover: We are reinventing health insurance by combining the power of data with human empathy to keep our members healthier. We believe the healthcare system is broken, so we've created custom software and analytics to empower our clinical staff to intervene and provide personalized care to the people who need it most.
We always put our members first, and our success as a team is measured by the quality of life of the people we serve. jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer
jobs.description:
Headquarters: Remote, Ontario, Canada


About CircleCI Engineering
CI/CD has been solved. Now it's being reinvented. AI agents don't just run pipelines. They write code, trigger builds, interpret failures, and propose fixes. The interfaces that developers use to understand and trust that work don't exist yet. We're building them.
At CircleCI, our guiding principles aren't posters on a wall. We learn fast: we run experiments, accept failure, and scale what works. We think like the customer: every decision connects back to the developer sitting in front of a failing build at 2 am. We own the outcome: not just our slice of it, but the whole thing. If that's how you already work, you'll fit here.
Team-Agnostic Placement
We don't hire for a team. We hire for CircleCI. Where you land depends on where your strengths create the most leverage, and we figure that out together. You might own the CI pipeline experience, deploy and release tooling, notification infrastructure, monetization flows, AI agent surfaces, or the foundational web platform. The through line across all of it is the same: full-stack ownership, a high bar for craft, and work that directly shapes how tens of thousands of developers experience CircleCI every day.
What You'll Do
Build AI-natively. AI is how we work. It's not a productivity layer on top of engineering, but the default starting point for how problems get approached and solved.
Set technical direction. You define the approach others build from. When the problem is complex or the answer isn't obvious, you're the person who leads the design discussion, writes the ADR, and makes the call.
Invent new interfaces. Software delivery is being reinvented. Pipelines run autonomously, generate fixes, and surface results that need human judgment. The tools developers use to understand, trust, and act on that work don't exist yet. You'll define what they look like and establish the patterns the team builds on.
Own the full stack. Build features end-to-end in Go, React, and TypeScript. You don't hand off at a layer boundary. You own the outcome.
Obsess over craft. Reliability and responsiveness are design concerns, not afterthoughts. Care about how the interface holds up when stakes are high and hold your team to that same standard.
Champion observability. Use Honeycomb, Datadog, and Rollbar to understand and improve your systems. Operational data drives stability, not just incident response.
Close gaps and fix the conditions that created them. You'll notice gaps and close them. When a gap reflects something broken in how the team works, you fix that too.
What You'll Bring
AI-native engineering practices. You use AI tools daily and can speak to what you've built, where they changed your approach, and where they fall short.
A track record of shipping. You've built something real and put it in front of users. 5+ years of production full-stack experience, with latency, responsiveness, and reliability treated as design concerns, not afterthoughts.
Full-stack depth. Strong React and TypeScript. Comfortable owning backend services in Go: API design, data modeling, service integration.
System design. You lead architectural decisions on complex systems. You make conscious tradeoffs, document your reasoning, and create the foundation others build on.
Adaptability. You don't just thrive in ambiguity, you reduce it for others. You turn unclear requirements into a direction the team can execute on.
Technical leadership. You mentor engineers, give direct feedback on technical direction, and raise the quality bar through how you engage in reviews and design discussions, not just what you ship.
Sound like you?
You've stopped waiting for AI to mature and are already building with it, not as a productivity trick, but as a core part of how you think about problems. You care about the product as much as the code. You're drawn to work where the patterns don't exist yet and the best answer requires you to invent it. If that's how you already operate, we want to talk.

jobs.title: Course Director: UX, UI, and AI
jobs.description:
Headquarters: Denmark
    
URL: https://ixdf.org/about/careers


You've been designing long enough to have watched tools become essential and then disappear. You know which design skills are timeless and which ones expire. The human-centered design skills are where your heart is, and you know that AI will take over much of the tool-based design work soon.
You see the fear around AI, and you understand where it comes from. But you also see the opportunities, and you want to show people how to work with AI in a way that benefits their lives, their users, and the world.
You can name the ten leading designers who should be teaching the world’s best courses and Master Classes right now. You know what each of them does better than anyone else, and where their gaps are.
Now you get the opportunity to decide what hundreds of thousands of designers learn next.
The industry leaders whose expertise you'll be turning into courses and Master Classes include Don Norman and Vitaly Friedman, as well as Design Leads at Netflix, LinkedIn, Meta, and Adobe. Don Norman also chairs our executive board.
You'll be involved in the entire process of creating our courses and Master Classes, and you'll lead many of the decisions, so there are incredible opportunities for you to take initiative, make meaningful contributions, and grow. Forget political struggles or long, pointless debates. You’ll be in a team with minimal distance between idea and action, where decisions are made ultra-fast.
Join the Global Leader in Online Design and AI Education
IxDF is the world's largest online design and AI education platform, with over 1,150,000 enrollments since 2002. We hold the trust of industry giants like Adobe, NASA, and IBM, who rely on our courses to train their teams. Prestigious universities, including MIT and the University of Cambridge, integrate our material into their curricula. Help us take online education to new heights and make a meaningful impact on humankind.
At IxDF, we’re not just a company but a movement dedicated to making high-quality design and AI education accessible to everyone, everywhere.
We've pioneered online design education since 2002. We have over 1,150,000 enrollments and 1,583 company members, with more than 40 courses, 160 Master Classes, and thousands of open-source design resources, created by our team in collaboration with 240 industry leaders.
With learners from over 100 countries, your work will empower people worldwide.
We're Hiring Three People for Our Editorial Team
We're growing, and three roles are open at the same time to build the next generation of our core educational product. Here's what each role leads on:
Our Course Directors, UX, UI, and AI: lead what we teach and who teaches our courses and Master Classes. You reach out to industry leaders and create the invitation they say yes to. You bring your judgment to a planned course outline: what's missing, what doesn't belong, and whether the structure is solid. You plan and shoot courses with our Education Designers. This is the role described here.
Our Education Designers, UX, UI, and AI: lead how design and AI are taught. You plan, structure, and create the core content, and you decide what a course participant should be able to do by the end and how they get there.
Our Course Writers and Editors: lead how our courses and articles read. You make each title engaging, ensure each sentence flows, and edit the written course experience from the user’s perspective.
We're a flexible team, and you'll be able to do what you excel in. Everyone on our team creates courses, and everyone works across these roles. If you're torn between two roles, apply for the one you'd be best at, and tell us in your application which other one you considered and why.
You, the Course Director, decide what belongs in our curriculum and who should teach it. You reach out to the world’s leading experts, plan the courses with them, and shoot courses with them. When an Education Designer brings you a course outline, you're the one who says what's missing, what doesn't belong, and how to optimize the learning outcome so designers can succeed today. You'll work closely with our Co-Founder, your Team Lead, our other Course Directors, and the Education Designers, and you'll plan and create courses alongside them. Our Course Writers and Editors take the finished material the last mile: the scripts, hooks, headings, on-screen text in videos, quiz wording, and editorial voice. You'll also work closely with the video team and our growth team.
Your Role at IxDF
Be a core part of our Editorial Team. You'll collaborate with IxDF editors, video editors, and UX and UI designers as well as external industry leaders to create courses and Master Classes for people worldwide. You'll help them succeed in the age of AI with new skills in AI and in timeless human-centered design.
You'll research what already exists in a topic area, so that what we build is genuinely unique. You'll look at where design and AI are heading, what designers need that nobody has taught well yet, and what we should retire because the field has already moved on.
Find the people who should teach it. You decide a topic is worth a course, you work out who should teach it and why, you write the email, and you get the yes. Then you plan the content with the industry leader and agree what the course must leave a learner able to do.
Decide what each expert should teach. The best designers know a great deal, and a course that tries to capture all of it becomes an information dump. You develop a point of view on what a designer genuinely needs from them, and you hold the course to it.
You'll decide which skills our courses teach, both to people entering design and to experienced designers leveling up. Our goal is to help designers thrive in the age of AI and work responsibly, so their users can thrive too.
Ensure our course participants finish each course with a solid portfolio project they can show a hiring manager.
Help us decide what AI should do for our course participants. Personalized learning paths, constructive AI feedback on portfolio work, practice environments where people run real design tasks and get feedback. You'll also help us improve the user flows on our own platform, so that learning at IxDF is as well designed as what we teach. You'll work on this with our founders, designers, and dev team.
Make an impact as you pressure-test the courses our Education Designers plan. An Education Designer sends you a course outline, and you read it against everything you know about the field and about how people learn design, then give constructive feedback on what's missing, what doesn't belong, and where the structure can be improved. You know the limits of your own expertise, and you research your way past them before you weigh in. You'll also plan, structure, and create courses yourself, alongside them.
You're one of the people whose judgment the rest of the team leans on. You show our Education Designers what ten or twenty years in the field taught you to look for. In return, our Co-Founder, your Team Lead, and our other Course Directors give constructive feedback on the courses you lead. You'll work in a diverse, highly organized, result-driven environment where you'll grow personally and professionally.
Act as guardian of our quality bar. When a course goes out under our name, it has to be better than anything else available on the topic. On the courses and Master Classes you lead or review, you're the one who spots what's not good enough yet and works with the team to fix it.
Bring your subject matter expertise to our writers, community managers, and social media team, so our design thinking stays consistent across everything we publish.
You help produce Master Classes. We produce 3 per month. Over email, you reach out to designers whose work you admire, invite them to create one with us, plan the content, and produce the live session. Timelines vary enormously: with Don Norman or Vitaly Friedman it can be two weeks from first email to publication, because we work with them often. With a new expert, it can be half a year. Once the session is recorded, you get the footage and the transcript, and you decide with the Education Designers and Team Lead which existing course benefits from which snippets, and where they go.
Focus on what matters as you take raw expert video material, course and Master Class transcripts and footage featuring global industry leaders, and turn it into educational material that teaches new skills in AI and in timeless human-centered design. You'll work across UX design, human-computer interaction, design thinking, UI design, psychology, and AI.

Fly out and meet the global industry leaders in design in professional studios across the world. You'll shoot the course content there with some of your colleagues. You know what the design community wants to see, and what it needs to learn.

You’re driven by the desire to make a positive impact in the world and to improve the lives of others.

You've spoken at design conferences, or you're on a first-name basis with people who do.
You've created design systems. Organizing complex material so other people can put it to use is a lot of what you'll be doing.
You've worked as an editor, or you've created online courses.
You have the graphic design skills to create image-based and interactive content for courses, articles, and social media.
You've built AI-supported learning tools yourself, or you've used AI to build products.
You hold a bachelor's or master's degree in UX, UI, HCI, AI, or a similar field.
You’ve collaborated with video production teams.

A highly valued role: You'll shape our core product, our courses and Master Classes.

A global, purpose-driven team: work remotely alongside passionate professionals from all over the world, united by a common mission to create the best possible design and AI education in the world and make it accessible for everyone.

A full-time position within a fully remote organization. Video-based collaboration with your colleagues from elsewhere on the planet, and we get together in person each year, on a team trip or for a studio production.
Bi-weekly knowledge-sharing sessions and 4 meeting-free days weekly for focused work.
A work culture with no fluffy titles, political agendas, or corporate drama. Your colleagues value your warm character, your strong work ethic, and the results you deliver. If you embody old-school virtues of always striving to deliver results, learn and become better every day, you'll thrive at IxDF.
A daily mission to help impact, empower, and enrich the lives of millions of people by creating affordable high-end design education for everyone across the planet. It'll be yours too.
Colleagues with four to forty years of experience, and a culture where we follow the best idea, not the longest résumé.
A company where the distance between idea and execution is minimal. We're a highly agile organization with zero bureaucracy or corporate politics – and with exceptional order and efficiency.
A company culture where passion meets high performance and excellence. To help us improve the world, and yourself in the process, you'll need grit, strong work ethic, long-term thinking, and self-discipline.
We thrive because we have a hands-on attitude and a bias towards action as opposed to fluff-filled, unrealistic strategies. You'll need crisp execution skills yourself and the ability to impress your colleagues with concrete results, just like they'll impress you.
We built online design education before people believed in it. AI is now changing what designers do, and they carry a bigger responsibility than ever. You'll be at the forefront of teaching designers to work with AI and to design responsibly for it. You'll help set a direction that shapes both the designers we teach and the people who use what they build. Together, we'll design a better world.

To submit your application as well as learn more about our Work Culture and Values, please visit https://ixdf.org/about/careers

That kind of judgment takes twenty years to build, and this type of collaboration is one of the fastest ways to grow your own design skills. Set and raise the standard for our assessments, so a correct answer proves understanding, not just recognition, and a good question teaches as well as tests. Our Education Designers decide what a question has to test. You write the wording that does both.
Balance the big picture with the smaller details. Expect to focus on one large course creation project per month, alongside small, continuous improvements to what's already published. You'll also write and edit articles, course descriptions, and supporting material, and help our Growth team and our two founders get the voice right in campaigns and social copy.
Turn expert material into lessons. Once you've built an understanding of design, you'll take a one-hour Master Class transcript and the learning goals for what the lesson must teach, then turn the strongest sections into a finished lesson. We produce 3 Master Classes per month, so new expert material arrives continuously.
Our courses combine written and video lessons. You'll work closely with the video team, giving constructive feedback on on-screen text, b-roll, graphics, and animation, and telling them which takeaways need a visual, so each video is more engaging to learn from.
Find room for improvement by looking at completion rates, learner feedback, and the portfolios learners produce, then go back and fix what isn't excellent yet. Small, incremental edits are why our material surpasses even the very best in industry and academia. We're always learning, always improving, always raising the bar in everything we do.
We’re committed to excellence, and we seek a like-minded enthusiast to join us. This role is not for the average. Ahead of you is a highly rewarding and enriching journey.
Maintain and improve our crystal-clear documentation so our knowledge resources stay up-to-date, easy to find, and provide instant value to our internal teams. Clarity is key. Any line of documentation should be self-explanatory.
You won't do this alone. You'll work with our Education Designers, Course Directors, your Team Lead, and our Co-Founder to pressure-test the material: you'll add what's missing, delete what's redundant, and suggest how to improve the structure. You'll be working with people who have anything from 4 to 40 years of design experience, ready to share their knowledge. We'll also help you upskill so you can grow a designer's eye alongside your editor's ear. You'll work in a diverse, highly organized, result-driven environment where you'll develop personally and professionally.
We're proud to have assembled a remarkable team of unicorns who uplift, motivate, and push each other to excel daily. There's a seat open for someone who shares our passion for excellence. Could that be you?
Do You Share IxDF's Vision?
People don't just buy our courses; they invest in a better version of themselves and a career they truly love. That's why every course we create and every sentence we write must do more than just inform. It must reflect the high-quality research and hands-on skills we teach.
Show the dream outcome: Help people imagine a future of creative, meaningful work, fulfillment, and impact through a career in design and AI.
Strengthen belief in success: Build confidence through real stories, practical case studies, and hands-on templates.
Overcome barriers: Write in a way that's crystal clear, human, and motivating. Connect and lead the way.
You'll educate, inspire, energize, and support. Whether you write a course article or give editorial feedback on a video, you'll help designers thrive in the age of AI.
About You
You have at least 4 years of professional writing or editing experience.
What matters far more than the number is the quality of the work you can show us: a course, an article series, a set of scripts, documentation, a newsletter. We’re excited to hear what it was, why you wrote it the way you did, and how long it took you to create.
You're a master communicator with a sharp eye for detail and strong skills in language, tone, and flow.
You can take a complex idea and write it so a beginner gets it on the first read.
You know how to hook someone with a title and a first line, and you know the difference between a hook that's earned and a hook that's cheap.
You collaborate with AI in everything you do. You use AI to write, research, and create faster, and you know how to take human leadership, so the outcome is 100% yours and better than you could have created without AI.
You’re eager to help people build UX and UI skills because you know they’re more relevant than ever in the age of AI.
You can write for a career changer and for an experienced designer without losing either one.
You have an exceptional talent for creating structure, and you take pride in organizing processes and tasks in a way that's efficient and clear.
You're genuinely curious about UX and UI design, and you're motivated to learn how great design shapes experiences and solves problems.
You're genuinely curious about how AI is changing design work and design education, and you look for new ways to use it in your own work.
You're kind, and you have the social intelligence and empathy to engage well with very different kinds of people.
You're fluent in written and spoken English, your grammar is exact, and you understand the power of tone, brevity, and microcopy.
You take full ownership of your work and see it through. You move comfortably across ad hoc projects of varying complexity, and you stay consistent when the work turns repetitive.
You’re enthusiastic about learning by doing and are committed to putting in the effort to continuously improve your skills.
You spot problems before anyone else notices them, and when something goes off track you come back with a solution rather than a report.
You value teamwork, prioritize collaboration, and focus on collective goals and harmony in the workplace.
You work well with great responsibility and freedom inside a well-documented, structured system. Accuracy and attention to detail are key on an online learning platform, where every tag must be correct and every piece of text formatted to our upload system. It's in your nature to meticulously double-check that everything is in order.
You're self-motivated, and you love creative freedom, independent judgment, and the responsibility that comes with both.
You’re driven by the desire to make a positive impact in the world and to improve the lives of others.
You're located in a time zone between UTC+0 (London) and UTC+4 (Dubai), which covers Europe, the Middle East, and Africa.
Bonus Points
None of these are required, but each of them would make us even happier.
You've taught in classrooms or workshops, or you've created educational material.
You have your own blog or social media page where you create and share original content.
You’ve collaborated with video production teams.
You've written quiz or assessment questions.
You've worked with an LMS or an online learning platform.
You hold a bachelor's or master's degree in communications, journalism, literature, or a similar field.
What We Can Offer
A highly valued role: You'll shape our core product, our courses and Master Classes.
Reach and impact that are difficult to find anywhere else in this field. Your words will be read year after year, by hundreds of thousands of people who build better careers and design a better world for all of us. An education you can't buy: free access to every IxDF course and Master Class, and a job that requires you to study the work of the best designers alive in order to edit it. Most people pay for this. You'll be paid for it.
Access: the designers whose books you'd normally buy are the people whose words you'll be shaping, and in some cases the people you'll be in a studio with.
Studio shoots: once you know our courses well, usually after your first year, you'll be a real asset on a studio production, and you'll be welcome to join us when we meet our experts in professional studios around the world. Some of us love that part and go every time; others keep travel to a minimum. Both work for us. On average we shoot 4-6 new courses per year.
Autonomy: Nobody will ever hand you a template and tell you to fill it in. You decide how our courses read.
A global, purpose-driven team: Work remotely alongside passionate professionals from all over the world, united by a common mission to create the best possible design and AI education in the world and make it accessible for everyone.
Our co-founder and co-CEO, Rikke, will work closely with you. She and our other co-founder, Mads, built IxDF from nothing, with no investment capital, so we would stay free to make world-class design education affordable to everyone. She was the sole editor and video editor for many of our early years, so she's shaped our course planning, expert interviews, video shoots, and content editing from the inside. She's still hands-on in everything we do, and she still films educational videos herself, in places like the US, the North Pole, and Nepal.
A full-time position within a fully remote organization. Video-based collaboration with your colleagues from elsewhere on the planet, and we get together in person each year, on a team trip or a studio production.
Bi-weekly knowledge-sharing sessions and 4 meeting-free days weekly for focused work.
A work culture with no fluffy titles, political agendas, or corporate drama. Your colleagues value your warm character, your strong work ethic, and the results you deliver. If you embody old-school virtues of always striving to deliver results, learn and become better every day, you'll thrive at IxDF.
A daily mission to help impact, empower, and enrich the lives of millions of people by creating affordable high-end design education for everyone across the planet. It'll be yours too.
A company where the distance between idea and execution is minimal. We're a highly agile organization with zero bureaucracy or corporate politics – and with exceptional order and efficiency.
A company culture where passion meets high performance and excellence. To help us improve the world, and yourself in the process, you'll need grit, strong work ethic, long-term thinking, and self-discipline.
We thrive because we have a hands-on attitude and a bias towards action as opposed to fluff-filled, unrealistic strategies. You'll need crisp execution skills yourself and the ability to impress your colleagues with concrete results, just like they'll impress you.
If you want even more opportunities to show the world what you can do, you’re in luck! When you're willing to do the hard work of learning and growing, then you’ll find virtually limitless opportunities with us.
We built online design education before people believed in it. AI is now changing what designers do, and they carry a bigger responsibility than ever. You'll be at the forefront of teaching designers to work with AI and to design responsibly for it. You'll help set a direction that shapes both the designers we teach and the people who use what they build. Together, we'll design a better world.
How to Learn More and Apply  
To submit your application as well as learn more about our Work Culture and Values, please visit https://ixdf.org/about/careers 
Please apply as soon as you can. We’re firm believers in “the sooner, the better” and we look forward to working with you!

Who we are
Typeform is a refreshingly different form builder. We help over 150,000 businesses collect the data they need with forms, surveys, and quizzes that people enjoy. About the Team
You'll join a small but high-impact Accounting & Controlling team at a pivotal moment in Typeform's journey.
As we've grown into a global SaaS business, our finance function is evolving to support greater scale, complexity, and ambition. We're investing in stronger financial controls, more sophisticated accounting operations, and systems that will enable our next stage of growth.
You'll partner closely with the VP of Accounting & Controlling, serving as their strategic deputy and helping lead both the day-to-day function and the longer-term evolution of our accounting organization. Reporting to the VP of Accounting & Controlling, you'll own the integrity of our global accounting operations, oversee a growing team, and drive initiatives that strengthen financial controls, improve efficiency, and support international growth. You'll combine technical accounting expertise with strong leadership and operational excellence, ensuring the business continues to scale on solid financial foundations.
This role is ideal for someone who enjoys balancing strategic thinking with hands-on execution. You'll be a trusted partner to senior leadership, mentor and develop the accounting team, and play a key role in transforming how finance operates across the company.

jobs.description:
Headquarters: Remote, Canada; Remote, United Kingdom; Remote, United States



GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.
The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.
*Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.

An overview of this role
As an AI Transformation Owner at GitLab, you'll shape your function's AI strategy and build the solutions that deliver it. You are the person responsible for identifying where AI can fundamentally change how your org operates, partnering with your Executive Sponsor to align on the biggest challenges, and driving measurable outcomes against them.
Think of this as a product management role where the product is your org's way of working. You'll manage the full lifecycle: understanding how work flows today, deciding where AI should reshape it, prioritizing what gets built and in what order, and ensuring what ships actually gets adopted. You'll also prototype solutions, configure agents, and prove what's possible before pulling in engineering support to scale it.
You will work closely with an AI Engineer who sits within the Enterprise AI team. Together you form a partnership: you bring the business context, process intelligence, and strategic prioritization. They bring the technical depth, production-grade delivery, and architecture decisions. You'll build working solutions at the no-code and low-code layer, and partner with the AI Engineer on the right approach, tooling, and structure.
What you'll do
Strategy & Prioritization
Own your function's AI strategy, aligned with your Executive Sponsor and business priorities. Understand which metrics matter to the org, identify what will move the needle, define how you'll measure impact, and track progress over time.
Map how work flows across your function end-to-end, including the handoffs upstream and downstream to other orgs. Identify where the real constraints are, not just the ones your team can see. Focus on the 100x problems: where could leveraging AI in a workflow let your org execute it orders of magnitude faster, or at 100x more volume than before?
Manage intake of AI requests, ideas, and pain points from across the function, including via your Champion network. Ensure every team member has a clear route to surface what they need, rather than building independently.
Prioritize strategically against business outcomes and executive guidance. Hold the line on priorities - we cannot change direction every two weeks - and ensure the AI Engineer's time is spent on the highest-impact work.
Adoption & Change Management
Reimagine, not just automate. Challenge your org to think beyond injecting AI into existing workflows. Work with Enterprise AI to spot opportunities to fundamentally rethink how work gets done.
Drive adoption and change management together with the AI Engineer. The best AI solution is worthless if nobody uses it. Create the channels, rituals, and feedback loops that make AI visible in your function: shared spaces for teams to show what they've built, regular office hours, onboarding for new hires, and celebration of wins. Own the rollout and iteration needed to make AI initiatives stick.
Coordinate with Enterprise AI to ensure your function benefits from patterns, tools, and learnings emerging across other parts of the business.
Build and bridge the Champion network in your function. Champions are the peer community that extends your reach beyond what you and the AI Engineer can deliver directly. From early in the role, identify and recruit Champions across sub-teams (5-10% time, formally agreed with their manager), run a regular Champion sync, host demos to the wider function, and act as their bridge to Enterprise AI. Champions are not your reports: you coordinate them, you don't manage them. Without this network, your reach is capped.
Hands-On Building & Agent Operations
Build AI agents using no-code and low-code platforms (e.g. Glean, Workato, similar tools). Go from idea to working prototype without waiting for engineering.
Author and iterate on skills files that define how AI agents behave. Refine instructions based on real usage and share reusable skills across the function.
Configure MCP servers and tools, giving agents access to the business systems they need. Partner with the AI Engineer on what to connect and how to do it securely.
Own your function's fleet of agents. Some agents will be used directly by people in your org. Those that aren't, you own. Either way, you're accountable for their performance: tracking KPIs, running evaluations after model or data changes, and iterating based on what you learn.
Expect to rebuild. AI tools and models evolve fast. The agent you built last month may need to be replaced, not patched. You should be comfortable sunsetting your own work when a better approach emerges, and helping your org stay current rather than attached to what exists today.
What you'll bring
Business & Strategic
Deep knowledge of your function's operations. You understand how work moves through your org, where it gets stuck, and why. You can trace a process end-to-end and explain how it connects to the teams around it.
Strategic prioritization skills. You've managed competing demands before and can make hard calls about what matters most. You think in terms of business outcomes, not activity.
A product management mindset. You naturally think about intake, backlog, iteration, and adoption. You're comfortable defining success metrics and holding yourself accountable to them.
Strong communication and influence. You'll be the person saying "not yet" to some teams and "think bigger" to others. You need the credibility and interpersonal skills to make both of those conversations land.
Cross-functional instincts. You default to understanding how your org's processes affect and are affected by the teams around you - not just optimising in isolation.
Experience building peer networks or communities of practice. You've recruited and sustained volunteer contributors before, whether as a guild lead, champion program owner, or community organizer. You know how to motivate people whose time you don't directly own.
Hands-On & Technical
Comfortable building with AI tools. You don't need to write production code, but you should be able to build a working agent, configure a skill, connect an MCP server, and troubleshoot when something isn't working. Think: power user, not software engineer.
Ready to learn fast. Experience with or willingness to quickly pick up no-code/low-code AI platforms, prompt engineering, and agent configuration. You'll be trained on GitLab's specific tooling, but you should arrive ready to get your hands dirty.
Strong conceptual understanding of AI capabilities - summarization, classification, generation, automation, agentic workflows - and a commitment to staying current. The landscape shifts constantly. The tools you use today may be obsolete in weeks. You stay on top of new developments so that your org's AI strategy reflects what's actually possible, not what was possible six months ago.
Ability to map data flows - structured and unstructured. Understand where agents need context, and figure out where humans should interface with automated workflows and at what steps.
About the team
You will partner closely with Enterprise AI within the Enterprise Technology & AI organization, while remaining embedded in your own function. Enterprise AI provides the technical delivery capability, platforms, and patterns. You provide the business context, prioritization, building at the no-code layer, and adoption muscle. Together, you form the core of your function's AI transformation.

jobs.title: Engineering Manager, Experimentation
jobs.description:
Headquarters: Remote - US


About the Job:
We're looking for an Engineering Manager for our Experimentation team. In this role, you'll lead the team that builds and operates the core Experimentation product, from setup to results processing and display.
LaunchDarkly’s Experimentation team is building one of the company’s most strategic product areas: a platform that helps leading engineering organizations move beyond intuition and make product decisions with real statistical confidence. Sitting at the intersection of large-scale systems, data science, and user experience, the team is creating a best-in-class experimentation product that lets customers set up, manage, and analyze experiments with ease while still earning the trust of even the most rigorous data teams. From warehouse-native analysis to experimentation workflows built on top of LaunchDarkly’s massive feature management scale, this team is tackling ambitious technical problems with visible customer impact and a clear opportunity to define the future of modern software experimentation
As the Engineering Manager, you'll bring a balance of people management and technical leadership as you drive the development of the multiple services that power this product and foster a high-performing, collaborative engineering culture.
Responsibilities:
Lead and develop a team of engineers, providing coaching, feedback, and career growth opportunities
Partner with PM and Design to scope, estimate, and sequence roadmap items, making scope tradeoffs in real time.
Own the team's delivery of features, ensuring completion within timelines and quality requirements.
Collaborate with adjacent teams (Warehouse Integrations, Metrics, and Guardian) on shared infrastructure decisions and cross-team dependencies
Communicate roadmaps, risks, and progress clearly to engineering leadership and cross-functional stakeholders
Build team working norms that promote collaboration, reduce silos, and keep engineers engaged
Drive operational excellence — improve reliability, observability, and incident response for production data infrastructure
Participate in hiring to grow the team and raise the engineering bar
Qualifications:
3+ years of experience in software engineering, with at least 2 years managing a team of backend or infrastructure engineers
Proven ability to partner with Product Management to translate business goals into engineering plans with reliable estimations
Strong communication skills, especially in distributed team environments with cross-timezone collaboration
Track record of coaching and developing engineers, including performance management, career growth planning, and technical mentorship
Familiarity with observability practices (metrics, tracing, alerting, structured logging) and comfort with production incident response
Experience with Go or comparable backend languages (Java, Python, Rust) is a plus
Familiarity with data warehouse platforms (Snowflake, Redshift, BigQuery, Databricks) and data pipeline tooling (Airflow, Prequel) is a plus

The LaunchDarkly platform helps developers innovate on new features faster while protecting them with a safety valve to instantly rewind when things go wrong. Developers can target product experiences to any customer segment and maximize the business impact of every feature. And by gradually rolling out new application components, they escape nightmare "big-bang" technology migrations. 
The LaunchDarkly platform was built to guide engineers to the next frontier of DevOps by:
Improving the velocity and stability of software releases, without the fear of end customer outages
Delivering targeted experiences by easily personalizing features to customer cohorts
Maximizing the business impact of every feature through the ability to experiment and optimize
Coordinating the release and optimization of software to provide consistent experiences across mobile platforms and device types
Improving the effectiveness and productivity of engineering teams, by providing insights into engineering cadence and stability
At LaunchDarkly, we believe in the power of teams. We're building a team that is humble, open, collaborative, respectful and kind. jobs.title: Senior Product Designer
jobs.description:
Headquarters: Poland - Remote



At INGENIOUS.BUILD, we have developed a top-notch platform for companies in the real estate and construction industries worldwide. Our platform enables companies to easily manage all aspects of their projects from start to finish, both internally and with other project participants. 

Joining INGENIOUS.BUILD means embarking on an incredible journey to create the first cloud application for managing the entire lifecycle of a real estate construction project. You'll be building what some consider the holy grail of construction project management.
